eventMetadata.context_description: Sweden's September 13 general election drives the market, with consistent polling through mid-August showing Magdalena Andersson's Social Democrats and the broader center-left bloc maintaining a lead of roughly four to eight points over incumbent Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson's right-wing Tidö alliance. Recent surveys, including Demoskop data released in August, place the opposition near 50 percent support while the governing bloc sits around 47 percent, narrowing slightly from earlier summer readings but preserving the structural advantage for a shift in government formation. Traders price Andersson at 83.5 percent and Kristersson at 15.5 percent as the implied probability of the center-left securing enough seats to form the next administration, consistent with historical patterns where the largest party in the leading bloc typically supplies the prime minister. Other listed candidates reflect marginal probabilities tied to smaller parties' influence in potential coalitions.

title: Eurozone Annual GDP Growth 2026
description:
This market will resolve according to the estimation of Euro Area (Eurozone) annual GDP growth for the full year of 2026 (% change), based on seasonally and calendar adjusted quarterly data, as reported in the "GDP and employment flash estimates for the fourth quarter of 2026" flash release for Q4 of 2026, scheduled to be released in January 2027.

The GDP release will be made available here: https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/main/news/euro-indicators

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher range bracket.

If no data for the Euro Area GDP growth rate for the full year of 2026 is included in this release, this market will resolve according to the Euro Area GDP growth rate for Q4 2026, as compared to the same quarter in the previous year. If no data is released for either the full year or fourth quarter of 2026 by the date the next quarter's data is scheduled to be released, this market will resolve based on data from the last available quarter, as compared to the same quarter in the previous year.

Note: data from the initial release of the referenced flash GDP report is what will be used to resolve this market. Data may be revised during the following quarter or as a part of the next estimate's publication, however any revisions to GDP report data made after the initial release of the specified report will not be considered for this market's resolution.

Recent data show Q1 2026 GDP expanding just 0.1% quarter-over-quarter, with annual rates near 0.8%, amid downward revisions by the ECB, OECD, and IMF to 0.8-0.9% for the full year due to elevated energy prices, lingering tariff effects, and soft external demand. Key upcoming releases on inflation, labor markets, and ECB policy decisions could refine these probabilities as fresh economic data emerges.

eventMetadata.context_description: Federal law fixes the date of U.S. midterm elections on the first Tuesday after the first Monday in November of even-numbered years, requiring congressional action rather than executive authority to alter or postpone. With Election Day set for November 3, 2026, and primaries already underway across states, no legislation or institutional process has advanced to change the schedule despite earlier speculation. Traders assign a 96% probability to the elections occurring as planned because historical precedent, separation of powers, and the absence of viable emergency powers support continuity. Remaining low-probability scenarios include an unprecedented congressional vote amid a severe national crisis or unforeseen constitutional disruption, though none appear imminent.

title: Bulgaria Presidential Election
description:
Presidential elections in Bulgaria are expected to be held in the Fall of 2026.

This market will resolve according to the listed candidate who wins the next presidential election in Bulgaria. 

This market includes any potential second round. If the result of this election isn't known by December 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, the market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the result of the election, as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the Bulgarian government, specifically the Central Election Commission (Centralna izbiratelna komisia, CEC) (www.cik.bg/).

eventMetadata.context_description: Iliana Iotova holds a commanding lead in the Bulgaria presidential election market as the acting president who assumed office following Rumen Radev’s January 2026 resignation to contest parliamentary elections. Her position strengthened after Progressive Bulgaria, formed by Radev, secured a parliamentary majority in the April 2026 vote, followed by official endorsements from that party and the Bulgarian Socialist Party in late July. An election date of October 25 was set shortly afterward, with recent polling reflecting broad public support around 50 percent. Andrey Gyurov trails as the appointed caretaker prime minister amid a fragmented opposition field. Lower-probability candidates remain sidelined due to limited visibility and organizational backing ahead of the vote.

title: UK Annual GDP Growth 2026
description:
This market will resolve according to the estimate of UK real gross domestic product (GDP) across the year of 2026 (% change) in the "GDP First quarterly estimate, UK" release for October-December (Q4) of 2026, scheduled for February 12, 2027.

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher range bracket.

The GDP release will be made available here: https://www.ons.gov.uk/economy/grossdomesticproductgdp/bulletins/gdpfirstquarterlyestimateuk/previousreleases

The estimate of UK real GDP across the year of 2026 is an estimate of the rate at which real GDP changed, on average, throughout the year of 2026. The relevant figure may be found in “Table 1: Headline national accounts indicators for the UK” under “GDP (Chained Volume Measures)” for the relevant year, or elsewhere in the release.

If no data for the estimate of UK real gross domestic product (GDP) across the year of 2026 is included in this release, this market will resolve according to the rate at which UK real gross domestic product (GDP) changed in Q4 compared with the same quarter of the previous year. If neither figure is released by the date the next quarter's GDP first quarterly estimate is scheduled to be released, this market will resolve based on quarterly data (compared to the same quarter in the previous year) from the last available quarter.

Note: data from the initial release of the referenced GDP report is what will be used to resolve this market. Data may be revised during the following quarter or as a part of the next estimate's publication, however any revisions to GDP report data made after the initial release will not be considered for this market's resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: UK GDP growth forecasts for 2026 cluster around 0.9–1.1% across institutions including the OECD, EY, OBR, and Vanguard, aligning with the market’s strong consensus on the 1–2% range. The latest ONS release showed 0.4% quarter-on-quarter expansion in Q2 2026, down from 0.6% in Q1, with annual growth at 1.2%, reflecting resilient services and investment offset by softening production and construction. Persistent drags from the Middle East energy-price shock, elevated inflation pressures peaking later in 2026, and widening economic slack have tempered momentum, while Bank of England communications highlight subdued underlying demand and limited policy easing. Traders appear to price modest recovery potential from consumption and fiscal support against downside risks from geopolitical supply disruptions and weaker global demand.

title: Anthony Albanese out as Prime Minister of Australia by...?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Anthony Albanese ceases to be the Prime Minister of Australia for any period of time between market creation and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

An announcement of Anthony Albanese's resignation/removal before this market's end date will immediately resolve this market to "Yes", regardless of when the announced resignation/removal goes into effect.

The resolution source for this market will be official information from the Australian government and Anthony Albanese; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

eventMetadata.context_description: Anthony Albanese secured a landslide re-election for Labor in May 2025, expanding the party's House majority to 94 seats and marking the first time an incumbent government increased its majority after a full term. The next federal election is not due until 2028, leaving the government with a substantial buffer absent a loss of parliamentary confidence or voluntary resignation. Recent mid-2026 polling has shown Albanese's net approval at record lows around -24 and Labor's primary vote hovering near 27-30 percent, with One Nation gaining ground and occasionally leading on primaries. No leadership challenge or procedural trigger has emerged to date. Traders assessing removal risks before year-end 2026 weigh these structural protections against any sudden internal party shifts or major scandals.

title: What chain will the NYSE choose for tokenized securities?
description:
NYSE has announced plans to launch a tokenized securities platform. More details can be found here: https://x.com/NYSE/status/2013263835549819097

This market will resolve to the blockchain that the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) officially confirms it will use for the settlement of its tokenized securities platform.

An official announcement, regulatory filing, or public statement from NYSE or ICE explicitly naming a blockchain will qualify for resolution and will trigger immediate resolution, regardless of whether additional blockchains are announced later.

If multiple blockchains are officially confirmed at the time of the first qualifying announcement, this market will resolve to “Multichain.”

If NYSE or ICE confirms the use of its own blockchain developed by or for NYSE/ICE—whether public or private, and whether developed independently or in partnership—this market will resolve to “Own Chain.”

The primary resolution sources will be official announcements from NYSE or ICE, regulatory filings, or a broad consensus of credible reporting.

If no blockchain is officially confirmed by December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to “Other.”

title: Predicted Fed rate under each Fed Chair
description:
This market will resolve according to the combined outcome of who will be confirmed as the next Fed Chair and whether the Fed’s lower bound will reach 2.5% or lower (https://polymarket.com/event/what-will-fed-rate-hit-before-2027) at any point by December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET.

This market will resolve to “Other” if an outcome not listed occurs within the specified timeframe.

This market may resolve as soon as the respective conditions are met.

The rules and resolution criteria are as follows:

1. Who be confirmed as the next Fed Chair?
This market will resolve according to the next individual confirmed by the U.S. Senate to be Chair of the Federal Reserve by December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET.

Confirmation is defined as approval by the U.S. Senate, whether by a majority vote or by unanimous consent.

Recess appointments without Senate confirmation will not count toward a "Yes" resolution.

Acting or interim appointments will not count unless the individual is confirmed by the U.S. Senate to be Chair of the Federal Reserve.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the U.S. Senate (see: https://www.senate.gov/legislative/nominations_new.htm); however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

2. Will the Fed’s lower bound reach 2.5% or lower in 2026?
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the lower bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal fund range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve according to whether the lower bound of the target federal funds rate reaches 2.5% at any point by December 31, 2026, 12:59 PM ET.

Emergency rate cuts and hikes outside the regularly scheduled meetings will be considered.

The resolution source for this market is the official website of the Federal Reserve at:
https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm.

Note: If the lower bound of the target federal funds rate reaches 2.5% before a new Fed Chair is nominated, it will qualify.

eventMetadata.context_description: Kevin Warsh's appointment as Fed Chair in May 2026 has coincided with persistent inflation above the 2% target, prompting the committee to signal a more hawkish stance through updated dot-plot projections that now point toward steady or higher policy rates through year-end. Recent FOMC communications and the median forecast rising to around 3.8% have reinforced trader views that borrowing costs will remain elevated, driving the 94% implied probability that the rate stays above 2.5% during his tenure. This consensus reflects the wisdom of crowds betting on data-dependent restraint rather than early easing. A sharp drop in inflation readings or clear signs of economic weakness could still shift expectations toward cuts and narrow that gap.

title: HUDL FDV above ___ one day after launch?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Fully Diluted Valuation of Huddle's governance token is greater than the value specified in the title 1 day after launch. Otherwise, the market will resolve to "No."

The token must be actively, publicly transferable and tradable to be considered a launch.

The FDV will be determined using the total token supply multiplied by the token price.

"1 day after launch" is defined as 4:00 PM ET on the calendar day following launch. The resolution source for this market is the most liquid price source available. If Huddle (https://x.com/huddle01com) doesn't launch a token by December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "No".

title: Argentina Official USD Exchange Rate end of 2026?
description:

Note: the resolution source for this market will be the Central Bank of Argentina (BCRA), which reports the Wholesale Exchange Rate to two decimal points (e.g., 1,408.02 ARS per USD). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

title: Trump x Greenland deal signed by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if both Denmark and the United States sign a deal, treaty, or similar international agreement of any kind relating to Greenland by December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Any U.S.–Danish agreement relating to Greenland will qualify, regardless of subject matter, including but not limited to sovereignty, governance, security arrangements, or access to natural resources.

Examples of qualifying deals include but are not limited to a treaty that makes any portion of Greenland a U.S. territory or possession (even if the handover date for such territory or possession is later); or, a Guantánamo-style arrangement treaty establishing a defined zone in Greenland under exclusive or primary U.S. jurisdiction and control, where Denmark and Greenland’s ordinary legal authority does not apply except by U.S. permission; or agreements permitting additional U.S. troop stationing, basing access, or resource extraction rights in Greenland.

This market will resolve to “Yes” only if a qualifying agreement is formally signed by authorized representatives of both Denmark and the United States. Official announcements, statements of intent, or declarations that an agreement has been reached will not suffice unless accompanied by signatures from both sides. Whether or not a qualifying deal is later passed by the respective parliaments or enters into force will not affect this market’s resolution. Signaling from Greenland’s population will not be considered.

Announcements, negotiations, proposals, frameworks, or understandings that are not formally signed by both parties will not qualify. Any qualifying U.S. jurisdiction, control, basing rights, or access arrangements in Greenland that existed at market creation will not count as new qualifying agreements.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the governments of the United States and Denmark; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Negotiations over enhanced U.S. access to Greenland have advanced slowly since the January 2026 framework announcement, leaving a full purchase or sovereignty-transfer agreement unlikely by year-end.** 

In early 2026, President Trump revived acquisition efforts, directing aides including Secretary of State Marco Rubio to explore a purchase while threatening tariffs on Denmark and European allies. Following talks with NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte at Davos, Trump dropped the tariff threats and described a “framework of a future deal” covering Arctic security, U.S. mineral rights, Golden Dome missile defense cooperation, and expanded basing—without immediate Danish or Greenlandic sovereignty concessions. Denmark and Greenland have stressed respect for existing sovereignty and autonomy, while cost estimates reached as high as $700 billion and procedural hurdles, including Danish parliamentary and Greenlandic consent, remain substantial. 

By mid-August 2026, no binding purchase or major transfer agreement has been signed despite ongoing trilateral discussions; existing defense pacts continue to govern U.S. presence. Traders therefore assign a 70.5% probability that no qualifying deal will be finalized before December 31, reflecting the pace of diplomacy, domestic political constraints in Copenhagen and Nuuk, and the complexity of Arctic security arrangements.

title: Brazil Annual Inflation 2026
description:
This is a market about the variation of consumer prices in Brazil over the 12-month period ending December 2026, as reported by the Brazilian Institute of Geography and Statistics (IBGE).

This market will resolve according to the percentage change in the Extended National Consumer Price Index (IPCA) during the 12-month period ending December 2026 according to the monthly IBGE report.

The resolution source for this market will be the IBGE Extended National Consumer Price Index monthly report released for December 2026, currently scheduled to be released on January 12, 2027. Resolution of this market will take place upon release of the aforementioned data. If no data for the specified month is released by the date the next month's data is scheduled to be released, this market will resolve based on data from the last available month.

You can find the relevant figure by locating the report for December 2026 on the Press Releases page (https://agenciadenoticias.ibge.gov.br/en/agencia-press-room.html), locating the Period-Rate table and finding the IPCA growth rate figure in the column labeled "Rate" and the Row labeled “Cumulative in the year / 12 Months”. Changes in the IBGE’s reporting format will not disqualify a published relevant figure from counting.

Note: the resolution source for this market will be the official monthly IBGE IPCA news release which reports inflation during 12-month periods to two decimal points (e.g. 4.26%). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market. For the full release schedule, see: https://www.ibge.gov.br/en/calendar.html

title: 2026 World GDP Growth
description:
This Market will resolve according to the estimate of the World GDP growth rate (Real GDP, annual percent change) reported by the International Monetary Fund in the World Economic Outlook Update released between the October 2026 and April 2027 editions of the World Economic Outlook, expected to be released in January 2027. 

The relevant figure may be found in the table titled “World Economic Outlook Growth Projections” under “Estimate” in the row “World Output” and the column “2026”. Changes in the IMF’s World Economic Outlook reporting format will not disqualify a published figure from counting.

The GDP release will be made available here: https://www.imf.org/en/publications/weo

If no estimate of the 2026 annual percent change in world real GDP is released in a World Economic Outlook Update between the October 2026 and April 2027 editions of the World Economic Outlook, this market will resolve according to the published figure for 2026 annual percent change in World real GDP in the April 2027 edition of the World Economic Outlook. If no such figure is published by April 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, another credible resolution source will be chosen.

If multiple World Economic Outlook Updates are released between the October 2026 and April 2027 editions of the World Economic Outlook, this market will resolve based on the first such publication which includes an estimate of the 2026 annual percent change in World GDP. Projections of World GDP, however, will not be considered.

Note: data from the initial release of the referenced GDP report is what will be used to resolve this market. Data may be revised during the following release or as a part of the next estimate's publication, however any revisions to GDP report data made after the initial release will not be considered for this market's resolution.

Note: the resolution source for this market reports annual percent change in world real GDP to one decimal point (e.g. 3.3%). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Key near-term catalysts include August and September inflation releases and central bank communications that could clarify the inflation-growth tradeoff.

title: Ledger IPO closing market cap above ___ ?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if the official closing price for Ledger's market capitalization on its first trading day is above the value specified in the title. Otherwise, it will resolve to “No”.

If no IPO occurs by December 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to “No”.

Market capitalization is defined as the total number of outstanding shares multiplied by the closing share price on the first trading day.

Resolution will be based on the primary exchange’s official listing page. In the event that the relevant figure is not displayed, another reliable source will be used.

In the event of an interruption in the course of the normal trading session on Ledger’s first day of trading (e.g., a circuit breaker or half-day), the market will resolve according to the official closing price of the abbreviated session. If no such official closing price is published, the market will resolve according to the next trading day on which an official closing price is published, treating that as the first day of trading.

title: Tariff increase on Canada in effect by...?
description:
On January 24, President Trump announced that the United States would apply a 100% tariff to all imports from Canada if a trade deal with China goes through. (see: https://www.reuters.com/world/china/trump-threatens-canada-with-100-tariff-over-possible-deal-with-china-2026-01-24/).

This market will resolve to “Yes” if an increase in the general tariff rate on imports into the United States from Canada goes into effect for any amount of time by June 30, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”. 

For the purpose of this market, "goes into effect" means the start date of the tariffs (as set by legislation or executive action) must have passed without being further delayed or suspended. Only tariffs which are in effect will qualify. Tariffs which are paused, or which have been announced but not yet gone into effect will not be considered.

Only tariffs specifically targeting Canada will qualify. For example, a new global tariff (tariffs on all imports into the U.S.) will not count toward this market's resolution.

The general tariff rate refers to the base tariff rate paid on imports, including any general tariff the U.S. imposes on all imports (e.g. a 10% tariff on all U.S. imports and a 50% tariff on top of that on Canadian imports would equal a 60% tariff). Item specific exceptions will not be considered (i.e. this market does not refer to the effective tariff rate). For the purpose of this market, an increase in the general tariff rate is defined as a rate greater than the rate in effect at the time of this market's creation.

A general tariff that includes item specific exceptions will still qualify, as long as a policy of a general tariff on all imports into the United States from Canada is in effect which is greater than the policy in effect at the time of this market's creation.

This market's primary resolution source will be official information from the Trump administration; however, a consensus of credible information will also be used.

eventMetadata.context_description: President Trump's July 20, 2026, proclamations under Section 338 of the Tariff Act imposed additional 50% duties on roughly $20 billion of Canadian imports, including dairy, alcohol, wine, cement, and other goods, scheduled to take effect August 19 unless altered by executive action. These measures respond to Canadian restrictions on U.S. products and build on prior escalations such as steel, aluminum, automotive, and forced-labor-related tariffs, many of which exempt USMCA-compliant goods. Bilateral talks have intensified in recent days, with Canadian officials seeking to avert or scale back the new levies while the U.S. side references retaliatory actions like liquor bans. Any negotiated pause, exemption expansion, or delay before mid-August would directly shape near-term resolution probabilities, while broader USMCA review dynamics and cross-border supply-chain pressures influence longer-dated outcomes.

title: Argentina Official USD Exchange Rate end of 2026? (Higher Brackets)
description:
This is a market about Argentina’s official wholesale U.S. dollar exchange rate at market close on the last business day of December 2026, as published by the Central Bank of Argentina (BCRA).

This market will resolve according to the official wholesale USD to ARS exchange rate (Tipo de Cambio Mayorista, ($ por USD) Com. A 3500 | Referencia) at market close on the final business day of December 2026, as published by the BCRA on its official website (https://www.bcra.gob.ar/).

If the official rate for that date has not been published by the end of the 7th day after the end of the specified month, the market will resolve according to the most recently published official wholesale rate preceding that date.

The resolution source for this market will be the official BCRA publication. Resolution will occur once this figure is available.

Note: the resolution source for this market will be the Central Bank of Argentina (BCRA), which reports the Wholesale Exchange Rate to two decimal points (e.g., 1,408.02 ARS per USD). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

eventMetadata.context_description: Argentina’s managed crawling-band regime, which adjusts the official ARS/USD band in line with lagged inflation, remains the dominant driver of end-2026 exchange-rate pricing amid the two leading brackets’ near parity at 42% and 34.5%. With the spot rate near 1,488 as of mid-August 2026, the Banco Central de la República Argentina has accumulated roughly $11 billion in reserves this year through daily dollar purchases while short-term rates have eased to the low-20% range, supporting gradual nominal depreciation that aligns with consensus forecasts of 1,760–1,850 by year-end. Traders appear to weigh the Milei administration’s fiscal surplus and export-led reserve gains against persistent monthly inflation near 2% and upcoming external debt service, creating tight implied odds between contained depreciation below 1,600 and moderate movement into the 1,600–1,700 band. Key near-term catalysts include September–December inflation prints and any adjustments to band expansion mechanics ahead of 2027 policy normalization.

title: Dreamcash FDV above ___ one day after launch?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Fully Diluted Valuation of Dreamcash's governance token is greater than the value specified in the title 1 day after launch. Otherwise, the market will resolve to "No."

The token must be actively, publicly transferable and tradable to be considered a launch.

The FDV will be determined using the total token supply multiplied by the token price.

"1 day after launch" is defined as 4:00 PM ET on the calendar day following launch. The resolution source for this market is the most liquid price source available. If Dreamcash (https://x.com/Dreamcash) doesn't launch a token by December 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "No".

title: Canada's population Up or Down this year?
description:
This market will resolve to "Up" if the population of Canada in the 4th quarter of 2026 is greater than the population of Canada in the 4th quarter of 2025.

This market will resolve to "Down" if the population of Canada in the 4th quarter of 2026 is less than the population of Canada in the 4th quarter of 2025.

If the population in the 4th quarter of 2025 and the population in the 4th quarter of 2026 are exactly equal, this market will resolve to 50-50.

If the relevant quarterly population estimate release is not available by April 30, 2027, 11:59PM ET, this market will resolve to 50-50.

The resolution source for this market will be the quarterly population estimates release for the 4th quarter of 2026 from StatCan (https://www.statcan.gc.ca/en/start). 

Note: data from the initial release of the referenced population estimate report is what will be used to resolve this market. Data may be revised during the following quarter or as a part of the next estimate's publication, however any revisions to population estimate report data made after the initial release of the specified report will not be considered for this market's resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Canada’s federal government released its 2026-2028 Immigration Levels Plan in November 2025, sharply cutting new temporary resident admissions from 673,650 in 2025 to 385,000 in 2026, including roughly 50 percent fewer international students and 37 percent fewer temporary foreign workers. Permanent resident targets stabilized at 380,000 annually. Statistics Canada data released in June 2026 confirmed the first quarterly population decline on record, with a 0.1 percent drop of about 55,000 people in Q1 driven by net outflows of non-permanent residents exceeding gains from permanent immigration and natural increase. Parliamentary Budget Office projections show flat overall population growth for 2026, as policy aims to reduce the temporary resident share below 5 percent of the total population by the end of 2027. These verified reductions in inflows and resulting outflows underpin trader consensus on a net decline for the year.

title: AK-AL House Election Winner
description:
This market will resolve according to the party of the candidate who wins the AK-AL congressional district seat in the U.S. House of Representatives in the 2026 midterm elections. The midterm elections will take place on November 3, 2026.

​A candidate's party will be determined by their ballot-listed or otherwise identifiable affiliation with that party at the time all of the 2026 House elections are conclusively called by this market's resolution sources. A candidate without a ballot-listed affiliation to either the Democrat or Republican parties will be considered a member of one of these parties based on the party with which they most recently expressed their intent to caucus at the time all of the House elections are conclusively called by this market's resolution sources.

This market will resolve based on the result of the election as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the United States government, specifically the Federal Election Commission (https://www.fec.gov/).

eventMetadata.context_description: Incumbent Republican Nick Begich III holds a strong position in Alaska's at-large House race ahead of the August 18 top-four primary, with the state's consistent Republican presidential voting history and his 2024 victory contributing to trader consensus favoring the Republican Party. title: Dutch House of Representatives dissolved in 2026?
description:

eventMetadata.context_description: The Jetten minority cabinet, formed in February 2026 after the October 2025 snap election and comprising D66, VVD, and CDA, entered office with 66 of 150 seats in the Tweede Kamer. It has since passed initial parliamentary tests, advanced targeted measures such as energy relief, and faces a scheduled election only in 2030. Traders therefore assign just a 7.5% chance of formal dissolution before year-end, viewing the coalition’s survival incentives and the absence of a viable alternative majority as the dominant stabilizers. Budget negotiations and opposition pressure could create volatility later in 2026, yet current parliamentary arithmetic and institutional continuity point strongly against an early vote.

This market will resolve according to the party of the candidate who wins the AL-07 congressional district seat in the U.S. House of Representatives in the 2026 midterm elections. The midterm elections will take place on November 3, 2026.

​A candidate's party will be determined by their ballot-listed or otherwise identifiable affiliation with that party at the time all of the 2026 House elections are conclusively called by this market's resolution sources. A candidate without a ballot-listed affiliation to either the Democrat or Republican parties will be considered a member of one of these parties based on the party with which they most recently expressed their intent to caucus at the time all of the House elections are conclusively called by this market's resolution sources.

This market will resolve based on the result of the election as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the United States government, specifically the Federal Election Commission (https://www.fec.gov/).

eventMetadata.context_description: Alabama's 7th congressional district remains a solidly Democratic seat due to its majority-Black demographics in the Black Belt region and consistent voting patterns favoring the party by wide margins in prior cycles. Incumbent Representative Terri Sewell advanced unopposed through the Democratic primary process, while Ammie Akin secured the Republican nomination in the August 11, 2026, special primary, leaving limited time and resources for a credible challenge before the November general election. Trader consensus reflects these structural factors, including incumbency advantages, low Republican turnout potential in the district, and absence of major recent developments that would shift the balance. A late-breaking scandal, health issue, or unusually strong national Republican wave could narrow the gap, though such outcomes face significant historical barriers in this district.

eventMetadata.context_description: Incumbent Republican Rick Crawford holds a commanding position in Arkansas’s 1st congressional district, where trader consensus assigns the party a 97.5% implied probability of retaining the seat. The district’s consistent Republican margins exceeding 25 points in recent cycles, combined with Crawford’s unopposed primary path and the Cook Political Report’s Solid Republican rating, underpin this positioning. Democratic nominee Terri Yarbrough Green faces structural headwinds typical of the region’s voting patterns and low Democratic baseline turnout. Late developments that could narrow the gap include an unforeseen scandal, health event affecting the incumbent, or an unusually strong national Democratic performance, though historical precedent and current ratings indicate limited scope for such shifts before November 2026.

This market will resolve according to the party of the candidate who wins the CA-10 congressional district seat in the U.S. House of Representatives in the 2026 midterm elections. The midterm elections will take place on November 3, 2026.

​A candidate's party will be determined by their ballot-listed or otherwise identifiable affiliation with that party at the time all of the 2026 House elections are conclusively called by this market's resolution sources. A candidate without a ballot-listed affiliation to either the Democrat or Republican parties will be considered a member of one of these parties based on the party with which they most recently expressed their intent to caucus at the time all of the House elections are conclusively called by this market's resolution sources.

This market will resolve based on the result of the election as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the United States government, specifically the Federal Election Commission (https://www.fec.gov/).

eventMetadata.context_description: Incumbent Democrat Mark DeSaulnier holds a commanding position in California's 10th congressional district heading into the November 2026 general election, following his strong primary performance where he secured nearly 60 percent of the vote. The East Bay district carries a deep Democratic partisan lean, reflected in its D+18 or stronger Cook Partisan Voting Index and consistent historical results favoring Democratic candidates by wide margins. Forecasters rate the race as Solid or Safe Democratic, consistent with trader consensus assigning the Democratic nominee over 90 percent implied probability. Limited Republican opposition, including nominee Jeffrey Frese, has not generated meaningful momentum in fundraising or polling. A major scandal, incumbent health event, or unforeseen national political realignment could theoretically narrow the gap, though structural advantages and the absence of competitive challengers make significant shifts unlikely before Election Day.

A Republican outcome would require unprecedented shifts such as a major scandal or turnout collapse, neither of which has materialized in recent cycles.

This market will resolve according to the party of the candidate who wins the CA-15 congressional district seat in the U.S. House of Representatives in the 2026 midterm elections. The midterm elections will take place on November 3, 2026.

​A candidate's party will be determined by their ballot-listed or otherwise identifiable affiliation with that party at the time all of the 2026 House elections are conclusively called by this market's resolution sources. A candidate without a ballot-listed affiliation to either the Democrat or Republican parties will be considered a member of one of these parties based on the party with which they most recently expressed their intent to caucus at the time all of the House elections are conclusively called by this market's resolution sources.

This market will resolve based on the result of the election as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the United States government, specifically the Federal Election Commission (https://www.fec.gov/).

This market will resolve according to the party of the candidate who wins the CA-28 congressional district seat in the U.S. House of Representatives in the 2026 midterm elections. The midterm elections will take place on November 3, 2026.

​A candidate's party will be determined by their ballot-listed or otherwise identifiable affiliation with that party at the time all of the 2026 House elections are conclusively called by this market's resolution sources. A candidate without a ballot-listed affiliation to either the Democrat or Republican parties will be considered a member of one of these parties based on the party with which they most recently expressed their intent to caucus at the time all of the House elections are conclusively called by this market's resolution sources.

This market will resolve based on the result of the election as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the United States government, specifically the Federal Election Commission (https://www.fec.gov/).

eventMetadata.context_description: California's 28th congressional district features longtime Democratic incumbent Judy Chu facing Republican April Verlato in the November 3, 2026 general election. Both advanced from the June top-two primary, where Chu secured roughly 62 percent of the vote in a district with strong Democratic voter registration and consistent historical margins. Forecasters rate the seat Solid Democratic, reflecting the area's partisan composition and the incumbent's established position since 2009. Trader consensus at 96.4 percent for Democrats aligns with these fundamentals and the absence of notable shifts in fundraising, polling, or candidate dynamics since the primary. Potential challenges include a late-breaking scandal, an unexpected national Republican surge altering turnout patterns, or other low-probability disruptions that could narrow the implied probability ahead of Election Day.

This market will resolve according to the party of the candidate who wins the CO-02 congressional district seat in the U.S. House of Representatives in the 2026 midterm elections. The midterm elections will take place on November 3, 2026.

​A candidate's party will be determined by their ballot-listed or otherwise identifiable affiliation with that party at the time all of the 2026 House elections are conclusively called by this market's resolution sources. A candidate without a ballot-listed affiliation to either the Democrat or Republican parties will be considered a member of one of these parties based on the party with which they most recently expressed their intent to caucus at the time all of the House elections are conclusively called by this market's resolution sources.

This market will resolve based on the result of the election as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the United States government, specifically the Federal Election Commission (https://www.fec.gov/).

eventMetadata.context_description: Democratic incumbent Joe Neguse holds a commanding position in Colorado's 2nd congressional district due to the area's strong Democratic lean, reflected in a Cook Partisan Voting Index around D+20 and consistent results in prior cycles. Neguse faces no primary opposition and benefits from high name recognition as assistant House minority leader, while Republican nominee Kelley Dennison emerged from a low-profile June primary in a district anchored by Boulder and Fort Collins. Trader consensus at 95% for Democrats aligns with the district's structural advantages and absence of competitive polling or fundraising signals for the GOP challenger. Scenarios that could narrow the gap include an unforeseen national Republican wave, late scandal involving the incumbent, or health-related withdrawal, though historical base rates in similar safe seats make such shifts rare before November.

eventMetadata.context_description: Republican incumbent Lauren Boebert holds a clear edge in Colorado’s 4th congressional district, an R+9 seat spanning rural Eastern Plains and southern Denver exurbs that ranks as the state’s most Republican-leaning. Boebert’s 2024 general-election win and uncontested 2026 primary, combined with the district’s consistent partisan lean, support the 64% Republican consensus reflected in trader pricing. Democratic nominee Eileen Laubacher, a retired Navy rear admiral, has outraised Boebert substantially and drawn national Democratic attention, yet nonpartisan ratings from Cook, Sabato’s Crystal Ball, and others classify the race as Solid or Likely Republican. The November 3 general election remains the decisive event, with no major late developments altering the underlying structural advantages for the GOP nominee.

eventMetadata.context_description: Republican Jeff Crank holds a clear advantage in Colorado’s 5th congressional district race, consistent with the district’s R+5 partisan voting index and its long history of Republican control in a Colorado Springs-centered area that has never elected a Democrat to the House. Recent developments include Jessica Killin’s primary win over Joe Reagan in June 2026, her inclusion on the DCCC’s Red to Blue target list, and Cook Political Report’s shift of the rating from Solid Republican to Likely Republican amid modest leftward demographic trends. A Democratic internal poll in July showed Killin within one point of Crank among likely voters, though broader polling remains limited and the district’s underlying partisan balance continues to anchor trader probabilities near 70% for the GOP nominee. Scheduled general election voting on November 3 leaves room for further shifts based on national conditions and turnout.

This market will resolve according to the party of the candidate who wins the FL-19 congressional district seat in the U.S. House of Representatives in the 2026 midterm elections. The midterm elections will take place on November 3, 2026.

​A candidate's party will be determined by their ballot-listed or otherwise identifiable affiliation with that party at the time all of the 2026 House elections are conclusively called by this market's resolution sources. A candidate without a ballot-listed affiliation to either the Democrat or Republican parties will be considered a member of one of these parties based on the party with which they most recently expressed their intent to caucus at the time all of the House elections are conclusively called by this market's resolution sources.

This market will resolve based on the result of the election as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the United States government, specifically the Federal Election Commission (https://www.fec.gov/).

This market will resolve according to the party of the candidate who wins the FL-24 congressional district seat in the U.S. House of Representatives in the 2026 midterm elections. The midterm elections will take place on November 3, 2026.

​A candidate's party will be determined by their ballot-listed or otherwise identifiable affiliation with that party at the time all of the 2026 House elections are conclusively called by this market's resolution sources. A candidate without a ballot-listed affiliation to either the Democrat or Republican parties will be considered a member of one of these parties based on the party with which they most recently expressed their intent to caucus at the time all of the House elections are conclusively called by this market's resolution sources.

This market will resolve based on the result of the election as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the United States government, specifically the Federal Election Commission (https://www.fec.gov/).

eventMetadata.context_description: Florida's 24th congressional district remains a safely Democratic seat with a partisan voting index around D+22, based on consistent past election margins and voter composition in northern Miami-Dade and southern Broward counties. Longtime incumbent Frederica Wilson announced her retirement in May 2026, triggering a crowded Democratic primary set for August 18 that features leading contenders such as state Senator Shevrin Jones and Miami-Dade Commissioner Oliver Gilbert; recent primary polling shows Jones ahead but the outcome has limited bearing on the general election. Minimal Republican filing activity and fundraising further reduce any competitive threat. Traders assign the Democratic nominee a 94% implied probability of victory because historical turnout patterns, district boundaries set in 2025, and the absence of crossover appeal make a Republican general-election win improbable. Late developments that could narrow this margin include an unusually strong Republican recruitment, court-ordered redistricting shifts before November 2026, or a sharp decline in Democratic primary turnout that signals broader base erosion.

The seat’s post-redistricting partisan lean favors Republicans, with historical voting patterns showing an 18-point Trump margin in the most recent cycle. Trader consensus at 84.5% Republican reflects the district’s structural advantages, incumbency, and limited recent developments that would alter the balance before the August 18 primary or November general election.

This market will resolve according to the party of the candidate who wins the GA-03 congressional district seat in the U.S. House of Representatives in the 2026 midterm elections. The midterm elections will take place on November 3, 2026.

​A candidate's party will be determined by their ballot-listed or otherwise identifiable affiliation with that party at the time all of the 2026 House elections are conclusively called by this market's resolution sources. A candidate without a ballot-listed affiliation to either the Democrat or Republican parties will be considered a member of one of these parties based on the party with which they most recently expressed their intent to caucus at the time all of the House elections are conclusively called by this market's resolution sources.

This market will resolve based on the result of the election as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the United States government, specifically the Federal Election Commission (https://www.fec.gov/).

Brian Jack, the sitting Republican representative first elected in 2024, advanced unopposed through the May 2026 primary, while Democrat Maura Keller secured her party's nomination. With the November 3 general election approaching, trader consensus aligns with the district's established voting patterns and limited competitive history. Shifts remain possible only in the event of a major scandal, health development affecting the incumbent, or an unusually strong national Democratic wave that alters turnout dynamics in this suburban and rural mix.

Incumbent Representative Hank Johnson secured the Democratic nomination in the May 19, 2026 primary with a clear majority against challengers Ansel Postell and Benedict Truman, while Republican James Duffie advanced unopposed in his primary. With the November 3, 2026 contest approaching and no evident competitive dynamics or major shifts in voter registration, trader consensus assigns overwhelming probability to the Democratic nominee. A realistic path for Republicans would require an unprecedented national environment or unforeseen candidate-specific event, both of which remain distant given structural factors.

McGowan, president of the Siouxland Chamber of Commerce and endorsed by President Trump, ran unopposed after Randy Feenstra retired to pursue an unsuccessful 2026 gubernatorial bid. Democratic nominee Dave Dawson, a former state representative who won a three-way primary, faces structural headwinds in a district spanning rural northwest Iowa including Sioux City and Ames. Nonpartisan forecasts rate the race Solid or Safe Republican. Late developments such as a major scandal, health issue, or unusually strong national Democratic turnout could narrow the gap, though historical margins and the district's voting patterns limit realistic paths to an upset.

This market will resolve according to the party of the candidate who wins the ID-02 congressional district seat in the U.S. House of Representatives in the 2026 midterm elections. The midterm elections will take place on November 3, 2026.

​A candidate's party will be determined by their ballot-listed or otherwise identifiable affiliation with that party at the time all of the 2026 House elections are conclusively called by this market's resolution sources. A candidate without a ballot-listed affiliation to either the Democrat or Republican parties will be considered a member of one of these parties based on the party with which they most recently expressed their intent to caucus at the time all of the House elections are conclusively called by this market's resolution sources.

This market will resolve based on the result of the election as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the United States government, specifically the Federal Election Commission (https://www.fec.gov/).

eventMetadata.context_description: Illinois's 1st congressional district remains a Democratic stronghold centered in Chicago and surrounding suburbs, where recent primary results reinforced party control ahead of the November 2026 general election. Incumbent Democrat Jonathan Jackson secured his party's nomination in March after defeating challengers, while the Republican side produced nominee Christian Maxwell without generating significant momentum. Trader consensus reflected in the 94 percent Democratic probability tracks the district's consistent electoral history, limited crossover appeal for GOP candidates, and absence of competitive polling or fundraising signals that would indicate a shift. A late scandal involving the Democratic nominee, an unprecedented national Republican wave, or unusually high turnout in Republican-leaning pockets could narrow the gap, though such developments have not materialized in available reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: The heavily Democratic lean of Illinois's 2nd congressional district, reflected in its partisan voting index and consistent historical margins, underpins the strong trader consensus favoring the Democratic nominee in the November 2026 general election. Robin Kelly's decision to pursue a U.S. Senate seat created an open race, but the March 2026 Democratic primary produced Donna Miller as the clear nominee after a crowded field that included Jesse Jackson Jr. The Republican nominee faces structural barriers in a district with limited GOP infrastructure and voter registration advantages for Democrats. Scenarios that could narrow the gap include a late scandal affecting the Democratic candidate, unusually low turnout, or a broader national political shift, though no such developments have materialized since the primary.

eventMetadata.context_description: Louisiana’s 2nd congressional district, anchored in New Orleans and surrounding parishes, maintains a pronounced Democratic tilt reflected in its partisan voting index and consistent electoral history. Incumbent Democrat Troy Carter secured reelection in 2024 with more than 60 percent of the vote and faces only limited intra-party and minor-party opposition heading into the 2026 cycle, including a primary challenge from Renada Collins and nominal Republican and Libertarian entries. Recent Supreme Court action in Louisiana v. Callais altered the state’s congressional map and primary procedures, yet the district’s underlying composition has preserved trader consensus around a Democratic outcome. A realistic shift would require substantial further redistricting before November, a major scandal or health development involving Carter, or an unexpected surge in Republican turnout that has not materialized in recent cycles.

This market will resolve according to the party of the candidate who wins the LA-04 congressional district seat in the U.S. House of Representatives in the 2026 midterm elections. The midterm elections will take place on November 3, 2026.

​A candidate's party will be determined by their ballot-listed or otherwise identifiable affiliation with that party at the time all of the 2026 House elections are conclusively called by this market's resolution sources. A candidate without a ballot-listed affiliation to either the Democrat or Republican parties will be considered a member of one of these parties based on the party with which they most recently expressed their intent to caucus at the time all of the House elections are conclusively called by this market's resolution sources.

This market will resolve based on the result of the election as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the United States government, specifically the Federal Election Commission (https://www.fec.gov/).

eventMetadata.context_description: Louisiana's 4th congressional district, encompassing northwestern areas including the Shreveport-Bossier City metro, maintains a consistent Republican tilt reflected in prior election margins exceeding 70 points. Incumbent Speaker Mike Johnson, who secured re-election in 2024 by 85.8 percent in a Republican-only primary, faces limited opposition in the 2026 cycle following the August filing deadline. Challengers include two Democrats and several Republicans, none of whom have shown substantial fundraising or polling traction. The district's nonpartisan primary on November 3, 2026, with a potential December runoff, reinforces trader expectations of a Republican hold. Factors that could alter the outcome include a significant late scandal, health event affecting the incumbent, or an unforeseen surge by a primary rival, though historical patterns and current candidate profiles indicate low probability of such shifts.

eventMetadata.context_description: Louisiana’s 5th congressional district remains a solidly Republican seat ahead of the November 2026 primary and potential December runoff, with trader consensus reflecting the district’s partisan composition and historical voting patterns. Incumbent Julia Letlow faces multiple Republican challengers in the state’s jungle primary, while Democratic candidates trail significantly in fundraising and name recognition. Nonpartisan forecasters rate the race Safe or Solid Republican based on consistent GOP performance in presidential and statewide contests within the district. Factors sustaining the high implied probability include limited Democratic infrastructure and the structural advantage for the party that has held the seat since 2019. Late developments such as a major scandal, health issue affecting the leading Republican, or court-ordered redistricting could theoretically reopen the contest, though no such events have materialized in recent months.

eventMetadata.context_description: Redistricting by Louisiana's Republican-controlled legislature in May 2026 substantially altered the 6th District's boundaries, shifting its composition toward stronger Republican performance and prompting Democratic incumbent Cleo Fields to withdraw from the race. Multiple Republican candidates have qualified for the November 2026 ballot in the reconfigured Baton Rouge-area district, while Democratic entrants remain limited. Forecasters rate the seat as Safe or Solid Republican, reflecting the new electoral math and absence of an established Democratic frontrunner. Traders assign the Republican Party a 94% implied probability of victory, consistent with these structural changes. Late developments such as an unusually strong Democratic primary performance or significant national political shifts could still influence the outcome before election day.

This market will resolve according to the party of the candidate who wins the MA-05 congressional district seat in the U.S. House of Representatives in the 2026 midterm elections. The midterm elections will take place on November 3, 2026.

​A candidate's party will be determined by their ballot-listed or otherwise identifiable affiliation with that party at the time all of the 2026 House elections are conclusively called by this market's resolution sources. A candidate without a ballot-listed affiliation to either the Democrat or Republican parties will be considered a member of one of these parties based on the party with which they most recently expressed their intent to caucus at the time all of the House elections are conclusively called by this market's resolution sources.

This market will resolve based on the result of the election as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the United States government, specifically the Federal Election Commission (https://www.fec.gov/).

eventMetadata.context_description: Incumbent Democrat Katherine Clark holds a commanding position in Massachusetts’ 5th congressional district, a seat she has represented since 2013 with margins routinely exceeding 30 points and a Cook Partisan Voter Index of D+24. The district’s consistent Democratic performance in presidential and state legislative contests, combined with Clark’s senior leadership role as House Minority Whip, has deterred credible Republican challengers; no well-funded GOP candidate has emerged ahead of the November 3, 2026 general election. Primary opposition from Jonathan Paz and Tarik Samman remains limited, with Clark favored at roughly 98 percent in related markets. All major forecasters rate the race Solid or Safe Democratic. Only an extraordinary late-cycle development, such as a major scandal or health-related withdrawal by the incumbent, would realistically alter the current trader consensus reflected in these prices.

eventMetadata.context_description: Massachusetts's 6th congressional district remains a reliably Democratic seat, reflected in the market's strong preference for a Democratic nominee ahead of the November 3 general election. Incumbent Seth Moulton opted not to seek reelection and instead entered the Senate primary, opening the race to a crowded Democratic field that includes Tram Nguyen, Dan Koh, and several other candidates ahead of the September 1 primary. The district's partisan composition, consistent Democratic performance in recent cycles, and limited Republican organizational presence in northeastern Massachusetts anchor trader expectations of continued party control. A general-election upset would require an unusually large national swing or primary fallout severe enough to depress Democratic turnout, outcomes viewed as low-probability given historical results in the North Shore and Merrimack Valley areas.

A national Democratic wave, significant personal or ethical controversy involving the incumbent, or unusually high turnout among opposition voters represent the primary, though low-probability, paths that could narrow the margin.

This market will resolve according to the party of the candidate who wins the NE-03 congressional district seat in the U.S. House of Representatives in the 2026 midterm elections. The midterm elections will take place on November 3, 2026.

​A candidate's party will be determined by their ballot-listed or otherwise identifiable affiliation with that party at the time all of the 2026 House elections are conclusively called by this market's resolution sources. A candidate without a ballot-listed affiliation to either the Democrat or Republican parties will be considered a member of one of these parties based on the party with which they most recently expressed their intent to caucus at the time all of the House elections are conclusively called by this market's resolution sources.

This market will resolve based on the result of the election as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the United States government, specifically the Federal Election Commission (https://www.fec.gov/).

eventMetadata.context_description: Incumbent Republican Adrian Smith, first elected in 2006, secured his party's nomination in the May 2026 primary with roughly 72% of the vote against a single challenger in Nebraska's 3rd Congressional District. The sprawling rural district, which encompasses most of western and central Nebraska and carries a strong Republican partisan lean, has consistently delivered large margins for Smith in prior cycles. Democrat Becky Stille and several independent and minor-party candidates, including recently certified nonpartisan Mark Cohen, are on the November ballot but face structural barriers in a district where Republican nominees have historically exceeded 75-80% of the general-election vote. Trader consensus at 95% Republican reflects the absence of competitive polling, fundraising gaps, or district-altering events, though late developments such as major scandals or turnout shifts could theoretically narrow the gap before Election Day.

Incumbent Democrat Donald Norcross secured the nomination without primary opposition and enters the November 2026 general election against Republican Damon Galdo, who also faced no serious intra-party challenge. Forecasters rate the seat Solid or Safe Democratic based on historical margins, voter registration, and fundraising patterns. eventMetadata.context_description: **Republican nominee Jeff Van Drew holds a strong position in New Jersey’s 2nd Congressional District heading into the November 2026 general election.** The four-term incumbent, who switched parties in 2019 and maintains close ties to former President Trump, secured his party’s nomination unopposed in the June primary. Democrat Zack Mullock, Cape May mayor, emerged from a four-candidate primary on June 2 to become the challenger. The district, which covers much of South Jersey including Atlantic City and Vineland, carries a Republican lean reflected in its partisan voting index and Trump’s double-digit margin in the prior cycle. Cook Political Report rates the seat Solid Republican, consistent with Van Drew’s 2024 performance and limited recent polling showing comfortable leads for the incumbent. These structural and electoral factors underpin traders’ consensus that the Republican nominee is the clear favorite.

eventMetadata.context_description: Herb Conaway, the Democratic incumbent in New Jersey’s 3rd congressional district, enters the November 2026 general election with a commanding lead after winning his 2024 race and facing no primary opposition. The district’s partisan voting index favors Democrats, and nonpartisan forecasters rate the seat Solid or Safe Democratic based on its suburban composition across Burlington, Mercer, and Monmouth counties. This market will resolve according to the party of the candidate who wins the PA-02 congressional district seat in the U.S. House of Representatives in the 2026 midterm elections. The midterm elections will take place on November 3, 2026.

​A candidate's party will be determined by their ballot-listed or otherwise identifiable affiliation with that party at the time all of the 2026 House elections are conclusively called by this market's resolution sources. A candidate without a ballot-listed affiliation to either the Democrat or Republican parties will be considered a member of one of these parties based on the party with which they most recently expressed their intent to caucus at the time all of the House elections are conclusively called by this market's resolution sources.

This market will resolve based on the result of the election as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the United States government, specifically the Federal Election Commission (https://www.fec.gov/).

eventMetadata.context_description: Incumbent Democrat Brendan Boyle's strong position in Pennsylvania's 2nd congressional district drives the market's overwhelming consensus for a Democratic win. The Philadelphia-area seat has delivered consistent Democratic margins exceeding 70 percent in recent cycles, supported by its urban voter base and limited Republican infrastructure. Boyle, first elected in 2015 and re-elected comfortably in 2024, faces Republican challenger Jessica Arriaga with no major primary challenges or redistricting shifts reported ahead of the November 2026 general election. Trader pricing aligns with this structural advantage and historical patterns in safe urban districts. Potential shifts remain limited to unforeseen events such as a candidate withdrawal, health developments, or an extreme national partisan swing that alters turnout in the district's core areas.

eventMetadata.context_description: Seth Magaziner, the Democratic incumbent first elected in 2022 and reelected with 58 percent in 2024, holds a commanding position in Rhode Island’s 2nd district, a seat under continuous Democratic control since 1994. Nonpartisan ratings classify the race as Solid or Safe Democratic, reflecting the district’s voter base in areas such as Warwick, Cranston, and parts of Providence. Magaziner faces a September 9 primary challenge from Spencer Dickinson but remains the presumptive nominee, while Republican contenders Victor Mellor and Stephen Skoly show limited name recognition and fundraising. These structural factors, combined with the absence of major recent developments that would alter the partisan balance, underpin the market’s 94 percent consensus for a Democratic general-election victory on November 3. Late developments such as an unexpected scandal or unusually strong national headwinds could still narrow the margin, though historical patterns indicate such shifts are rare in this district.

eventMetadata.context_description: Incumbent Democrat Jim Clyburn secured the Democratic nomination for South Carolina’s 6th congressional district with over 90 percent of the primary vote in June 2026, while Republican John Peterson advanced as the GOP nominee. The district’s demographics, including its Black Belt population centers around Columbia and North Charleston, have consistently supported Democratic candidates, with Clyburn winning reelection by double-digit margins in recent cycles. An earlier Republican-led effort to redraw congressional maps and target the seat collapsed in the state Senate during May 2026, leaving the existing boundaries in place for the November general election. This combination of incumbency advantages, primary results, and the absence of successful redistricting has produced the current trader consensus favoring the Democratic nominee. Late developments such as health concerns for Clyburn or an unforeseen national political shift could still alter the race dynamics before Election Day.

eventMetadata.context_description: Texas's 8th congressional district remains a strongly Republican-leaning seat, reflected in trader consensus favoring the Republican nominee at 93.5% implied probability. The open seat, created by Morgan Luttrell's retirement, features Republican Jessica Steinmann against Democrat Laura Jones in the November 2026 general election. The district delivered 63% support for the Republican presidential candidate in 2024 and maintains consistent GOP advantages in exurban Houston and surrounding counties. Steinmann secured the nomination in the March 2026 primary with backing from party figures, while Jones advanced on the Democratic side. With no major recent developments altering the fundamentals, the race aligns with historical patterns for this district. This market will resolve according to the party of the candidate who wins the TX-22 congressional district seat in the U.S. House of Representatives in the 2026 midterm elections. The midterm elections will take place on November 3, 2026.

​A candidate's party will be determined by their ballot-listed or otherwise identifiable affiliation with that party at the time all of the 2026 House elections are conclusively called by this market's resolution sources. A candidate without a ballot-listed affiliation to either the Democrat or Republican parties will be considered a member of one of these parties based on the party with which they most recently expressed their intent to caucus at the time all of the House elections are conclusively called by this market's resolution sources.

This market will resolve based on the result of the election as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the United States government, specifically the Federal Election Commission (https://www.fec.gov/).

eventMetadata.context_description: Texas's 22nd congressional district remains a solidly Republican seat following recent redistricting that strengthened GOP margins across the state. With incumbent Troy Nehls retiring, the Republican primary produced a clear nominee who enters the general election with strong party infrastructure and fundraising advantages typical of safe districts. Forecasters rate the race Lean or Likely Republican, reflecting consistent historical voting patterns and limited Democratic infrastructure in the suburban Houston area. Trader consensus at 92.5% Republican aligns with these structural factors. A Democratic upset would require an unusually large national midterm wave, significant Republican candidate vulnerabilities, or turnout surges among key voting blocs that exceed recent election benchmarks.

eventMetadata.context_description: Republican incumbent Beth Van Duyne holds a strong position in Texas’s 24th congressional district ahead of the November 2026 general election. Forecasters rate the contest Solid R, citing the district’s consistent Republican tilt and the incumbent’s established fundraising and name recognition. With no major recent developments or competitive polling shifts reported since the primaries, trader consensus reflects the structural and historical advantages favoring the Republican nominee.

This market will resolve according to the party of the candidate who wins the VA-03 congressional district seat in the U.S. House of Representatives in the 2026 midterm elections. The midterm elections will take place on November 3, 2026.

​A candidate's party will be determined by their ballot-listed or otherwise identifiable affiliation with that party at the time all of the 2026 House elections are conclusively called by this market's resolution sources. A candidate without a ballot-listed affiliation to either the Democrat or Republican parties will be considered a member of one of these parties based on the party with which they most recently expressed their intent to caucus at the time all of the House elections are conclusively called by this market's resolution sources.

This market will resolve based on the result of the election as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the United States government, specifically the Federal Election Commission (https://www.fec.gov/).

Historical margins exceeding 30 points and the absence of competitive dynamics or major recent developments have reinforced expectations of continuity into the November 2026 general election. Late developments such as a significant scandal, health issue affecting the incumbent, or an unexpected national political shift could still narrow the margin, though such scenarios remain low-probability based on available evidence.

This market will resolve according to the party of the candidate who wins the WA-04 congressional district seat in the U.S. House of Representatives in the 2026 midterm elections. The midterm elections will take place on November 3, 2026.

​A candidate's party will be determined by their ballot-listed or otherwise identifiable affiliation with that party at the time all of the 2026 House elections are conclusively called by this market's resolution sources. A candidate without a ballot-listed affiliation to either the Democrat or Republican parties will be considered a member of one of these parties based on the party with which they most recently expressed their intent to caucus at the time all of the House elections are conclusively called by this market's resolution sources.

This market will resolve based on the result of the election as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the United States government, specifically the Federal Election Commission (https://www.fec.gov/).

eventMetadata.context_description: Washington's 4th congressional district maintains a solid Republican tilt, reflected in its R+10 partisan voting index and consistent ratings as Solid R or Safe R across major forecasters. The open-seat dynamic following incumbent Dan Newhouse's retirement announcement has not altered the underlying dynamics in this rural, agricultural district encompassing Yakima and the Tri-Cities. The August 4, 2026, top-two primary advanced Republican Yakima County Commissioner Amanda McKinney and Democrat John Duresky, establishing a clear partisan general-election matchup on November 3. Trader consensus at 91.5% for the Republican nominee aligns with these structural factors and historical voting patterns. Late developments such as national political shifts, candidate-specific controversies, or unusually high Democratic turnout could narrow the margin, though such scenarios remain low-probability given the district's baseline.

This market will resolve according to the party of the candidate who wins the WA-09 congressional district seat in the U.S. House of Representatives in the 2026 midterm elections. The midterm elections will take place on November 3, 2026.

​A candidate's party will be determined by their ballot-listed or otherwise identifiable affiliation with that party at the time all of the 2026 House elections are conclusively called by this market's resolution sources. A candidate without a ballot-listed affiliation to either the Democrat or Republican parties will be considered a member of one of these parties based on the party with which they most recently expressed their intent to caucus at the time all of the House elections are conclusively called by this market's resolution sources.

This market will resolve based on the result of the election as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the United States government, specifically the Federal Election Commission (https://www.fec.gov/).

Trader consensus on Polymarket aligns with these structural factors and historical voting patterns in the Seattle-area suburbs. A significant shift would require an unusual national political realignment or unforeseen candidate-specific developments before Election Day.
